"'''If You're Gone'''" is a song by American [[rock music|rock]] band [[Matchbox Twenty]]. The song, written by the band's frontman, [[Rob Thomas (musician)|Rob Thomas]], was included on their second studio album, ''[[Mad Season (Matchbox Twenty album)|Mad Season]]'' (2000). In the United States, it was released alongside "Crutch" as the album's second and third single simultaneously on September 18, 2000—"If You're Gone" was sent to pop radio while "Crutch" was sent to rock formats.<ref name="gavin">{{cite magazine|title=Impact Dates|magazine=[[Gavin Report]]|issue=2322|pages=10, 33, 52|date=September 15, 2000}}</ref><ref name="r&r"/> "If You're Gone" reached number five on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart and also became a hit on [[adult contemporary]] radio, spending two weeks at number one on the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Adult Contemporary (chart)|Adult Contemporary]] chart.

"If You're Gone" is a song by American rock band Matchbox Twenty. The song, written by the band's frontman, Rob Thomas, was included on their second studio album, Mad Season (2000). In the United States, it was released alongside "Crutch" as the album's second and third single simultaneously on September 18, 2000—"If You're Gone" was sent to pop radio while "Crutch" was sent to rock formats. "If You're Gone" reached number five on the US Billboard Hot 100 chart and also became a hit on adult contemporary radio, spending two weeks at number one on the Billboard Adult Contemporary chart.

sections.heading: Background and writing
sections.wikitext: Rob Thomas told ''Billboard'' magazine that he wrote the song right after he met his future wife. "We were separated for a few weeks and were on the phone all the time, and I was thinking, 'I met this wonderful person', and I wondered if everything I was going through [with Matchbox Twenty's success] was going to make it too crazy to build a relationship."<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/00s/2000/BB-2000-04-01.pdf|title='Mad Season' Reflects on Relationships|last=Newman|first=Melinda|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|volume=112|issue=14|page=103|date=April 1, 2000|access-date=May 25, 2021}}</ref>

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
In the United States, "If You're Gone" debuted at number 52 on the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Billboard Hot 100|Hot 100]] on the issue dated October 21, 2000.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/2000-10-21|title=The Hot 100 – Week of October 21, 2000|magazine=Billboard|date=October 21, 2000|access-date=November 30, 2020}}</ref> It began to rise up the chart, eventually reaching a peak of number five on January 27, 2001.<ref name="hot100"/> As of {{YEAR}}, it is tied with "[[Unwell]]" as the band's second-highest-charting single on the Hot 100, and it is also their second-longest-staying single (behind "Unwell"), remaining on the listing for 42 weeks.<ref name="hot100"/> It was the sixth-most-successful single of 2001 in the US.<ref name="usye"/> On the ''Billboard'' [[Adult Contemporary (chart)|Hot Adult Contemporary Tracks]] chart, it stayed at number one for two nonconsecutive weeks in 2001,<ref name="usac"/> and on the [[Adult Top 40]] listing, it held the top spot for 13 issues, from December 13, 2000, to March 17, 2001.<ref name="usaps"/><ref name="Whitburn">[[Joel Whitburn|Whitburn, Joel]] (2004). ''The Billboard Book of Top 40 Hits'', 8th Edition (Billboard Publications)</ref> In Canada, the single peaked at number 27 on the ''[[RPM (magazine)|RPM]]'' 100 Hit Tracks chart before the magazine ceased publication;<ref name="can"/> because it was not released on a [[Physical single|physical format]] in Canada, it did not appear on the [[Canadian Singles Chart]].<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/matchbox-twenty/chart-history/CNS|title=Matchbox Twenty Chart History (Canadian Digital Songs)|magazine=Billboard|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191222071240/https://www.billboard.com/music/matchbox-twenty/chart-history/CNS|archive-date=December 22, 2019|access-date=November 30, 2020}}</ref>

Worldwide, the song found the most success in New Zealand. Despite peaking at number 12 on the [[New Zealand Singles Chart|RIANZ Singles Chart]], it remained in the top 50 for 34 weeks between November 2000 and July 2001.<ref name="nz"/> At the end of 2001, it was ranked as New Zealand's 11th-best-performing song.<ref name="nzye"/> On the Australian [[ARIA Singles Chart]], the song first appeared at number 48 on October 29, 2000, and took 13 more weeks to reach its peak position of number 18.<ref name="aus"/> In Europe, "If You're Gone" was a top-40 hit in Ireland, where it reached number 36,<ref name="ire"/> but charted weakly elsewhere, peaking at number 50 in the United Kingdom,<ref name="uk"/> number 84 in Germany,<ref name="ger"/> and number 95 in the Netherlands.<ref name="d100"/> In 2019, the song experienced a resurgence of popularity in Japan, reaching number 84 on the [[Japan Hot 100]].<ref name="jpn"/>
sections.text:
In the United States, "If You're Gone" debuted at number 52 on the Billboard Hot 100 on the issue dated October 21, 2000. It began to rise up the chart, eventually reaching a peak of number five on January 27, 2001. As of {{YEAR}}, it is tied with "Unwell" as the band's second-highest-charting single on the Hot 100, and it is also their second-longest-staying single (behind "Unwell"), remaining on the listing for 42 weeks. It was the sixth-most-successful single of 2001 in the US. On the Billboard Hot Adult Contemporary Tracks chart, it stayed at number one for two nonconsecutive weeks in 2001, and on the Adult Top 40 listing, it held the top spot for 13 issues, from December 13, 2000, to March 17, 2001. In Canada, the single peaked at number 27 on the RPM 100 Hit Tracks chart before the magazine ceased publication; because it was not released on a physical format in Canada, it did not appear on the Canadian Singles Chart.

Worldwide, the song found the most success in New Zealand. Despite peaking at number 12 on the RIANZ Singles Chart, it remained in the top 50 for 34 weeks between November 2000 and July 2001. At the end of 2001, it was ranked as New Zealand's 11th-best-performing song. On the Australian ARIA Singles Chart, the song first appeared at number 48 on October 29, 2000, and took 13 more weeks to reach its peak position of number 18. In Europe, "If You're Gone" was a top-40 hit in Ireland, where it reached number 36, but charted weakly elsewhere, peaking at number 50 in the United Kingdom, number 84 in Germany, and number 95 in the Netherlands. In 2019, the song experienced a resurgence of popularity in Japan, reaching number 84 on the Japan Hot 100.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The music video for the song, directed by Pedro Romhanyi,<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-Billboard/00s/2000/BB-2000-09-30.pdf|title=Production Notes|magazine=Billboard|volume=112|issue=40|page=89|date=September 30, 2000|access-date=October 8, 2020}}</ref> is filmed completely in black and white and features only the band (along with two [[trumpet]] players and a [[trombone]] player), performing at night on the rooftop of a building in the central business district of downtown Los Angeles. Halfway through the video, Rob Thomas steps onto the edge of the roof and spreads his arms like he's going to jump. He doesn't; he turns around and goes back to where the band is playing. Near the end of the video, the sun dawns and illuminates the rooftop and surrounding buildings of the city.
